title: District Commission's Power to Require Information

content.scenario: A consumer files a complaint against an e-commerce company with the District Commission. The Commission requires the company to provide information, documents, or records to investigate the complaint.
content.outcome: The District Commission may order the e-commerce company to provide the required information, documents, or records for the purposes of sub-sections (2) and (3) of Section 38 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

user_queries: What information can the District Commission require from an e-commerce company?
Can the District Commission order an e-commerce company to provide documents?
What is the purpose of the District Commission's power to require information?
